samples.question: This page shows two black figures far apart, one on each side, together with grey decorations. Grey never counts. One black figure is a strand that snakes back and forth; a few visible gaps are cut right through it, so it falls into separate pieces, and two parts belong to the same piece only when black ink joins them along the strand. The other black figure is a frame of two long rails crossed by several bars; a bar that reaches both rails closes off a white loop, while a bar that stops short of the far rail closes nothing, so the number of loops is the number of white areas the frame surrounds completely. Count the pieces of the strand and the loops of the frame. Which side of the page each figure sits on, figure size, bar count, gap positions and total ink are all irrelevant. Does the strand have exactly as many pieces as the frame has loops? Answer yes or no.
